newsitem.title: USA: Former Miami finance director sues city - paper.
newsitem.headline: Former Miami finance director sues city - paper.

text.p: Former Miami Finance Director Manohar Surana, who resigned to face federal corruption charges, has filed a lawsuit challenging the city's decision to withhold his pension payments, the Miami Herald reported Monday.
Surana, 52, resigned last August and subsequently pleaded guilty to sealed charges stemming from a kickback scheme involving city contracts.
Florida law requires forfeiture of a public employee's pension if the employee is convicted of certain crimes, including bribery, embezzlement and theft.

Assistant City Manager Robert Nachlinger said the city cannot accept or reject Surana's pension claim until the pension board learns what charges he pleaded guilty to. The payments are being held in escrow until a decision is made.

Surana filed suit in Dade County Circuit Court last week, claming the city had illegally withheld his $6,300 monthly pension payments. He also asked the court to reinstate a phantom raise that city officials said artificially inflated Surana's pension benefits.

Surana earned $109,999.97 a year but former City Manager Cesar Odio, who also resigned and pleaded guilty to corruption charges, had listed Surana's salary as $154,000 on city pension documents. That raise was revoked by Odio's successor.
